chapter_title: Concerning the Five Things that he constructed with the hard Bodies of the Rulers
chapter_note: This is a remarkably clean substrate chapter — a brief, systematic five-fold cosmological enumeration with minimal editorial overlay. The only non-substrate material is the dialogue frame attribution in paragraph 1. The teaching maps demon body parts (veins, skulls) to cosmic architectural structures (disc, arches, mould, pillars, walls). Both sides of every mapping stay entirely within the cosmic system. No editorial bridge, no institutional content, no exhortation. paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit constructed five great things from veins and skull[s in the] hard [bodies].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again the enlightener speaks:' — pure dialogue frame attribution formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Standard dialogue frame wrapper around substantive cosmological content. The teaching itself introduces the five-fold enumeration and names the cosmic agent (Living Spirit) and the material (veins, skulls of rulers' hard bodies). This is the setup for the systematic mapping that follows.

paragraphs.core_text: The first is the disc that is placed upon [the sh]oulder of the Porter.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First element of the five-fold enumeration. Maps construction from demon bodies → cosmic disc on the Porter's shoulder. Both sides internal to the cosmic system. The Porter (Omophoros/Atlas figure) is a cosmological being in the Manichaean cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: The se[con]d are the arches of [the] pillar that is before him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second element. Maps to cosmic architectural structure (arches of the pillar). Lacunae suggest manuscript damage but the teaching structure is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: [The th]ird is the [mou]ld of the fo[r]m for the gehennas.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third element. 'Gehennas' here functions as a cosmological location (zones of containment for dark matter), not as a moral/eschatological concept. The substrate score (27.27) confirms cosmological vocabulary. The 'mould of the form' suggests a template/pattern for cosmic containment structures.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth are the [seven (?)] pillars that he has erected in the great sea, in [the] seven parts of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth element. Maps to cosmic pillars in the great sea, distributed across seven parts of the universe. Seven-fold division of cosmic space is systematic cosmological architecture. The '(?)' indicates editorial uncertainty about the restored number.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth are the four walls that surround the vessels.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth and final element completing the enumeration. Four walls surrounding cosmic vessels. The 'vessels' are cosmic containers — part of the systematic cosmic architecture vocabulary (conduits, vessels, wheels). Clean closure of the five-fold teaching with no editorial extension.
